selected_result: Theorem 3.1: probabilistic componentwise backward error for a rounded inner product

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

task_clarification: For a,b in R^n, let y=a^T*b be evaluated in floating-point arithmetic in any permitted order, yielding yHat.
Assume the source relative-error operation rule and Model 2.1: the operation errors are independent, mean-zero, and bounded by the unit roundoff u.

For every lambda>0, on one event of probability at least Q(lambda,n)=1-n*(1-P(lambda)), yHat must admit both representations yHat=(a+DeltaA)^T*b=a^T*(b+DeltaB) with |DeltaA|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|a| and |DeltaB|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|b| componentwise.
Use exactly the source definitions of gammaTilde_n and P(lambda) in equations (2.1)-(2.2).
scope_constraints: The existential perturbations must be witnessed inside the same high-probability event; neither representation may be dropped.
Quantify over the source's allowed evaluation orders and keep the componentwise meaning of all vector inequalities.
Do not put the desired backward representation or event probability into the execution model as a hypothesis.
